language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.

Hi! My name is Karin and I live in Copenhagen, Denmark. I'm at Langelinie promenade in the Inner Harbour. This is where the canal tours sail. It's also home to our famous bronze statue, the Little Mermaid.

Copenhagen is also famous for people riding bikes. But it wasn't always like this. For many years, the water in the harbour was polluted and there was no place to swim or ride bikes. So we decided to clean it up. Now we enjoy city gardens and swimming in clean water. And 9,100 cyclists use the pedestrians bridge every day!
Farmers near by supply our restaurants with local produce. That is why our city was chosen the European Green Capital for 2014.
Let's explore more types of natural resources and why they are important to us.
Welcome to Denmark!

The effect of manufacturing fossil fuels can be devastating to our environment. For example, a coal is burned to make electricity. When coal is burned, the coal ash contains dangerous substances such as arsenic, mercury, lead and thallium. These toxic substances then contaminate our water supply.
Can you help me create my next webpage about how manufacturing industries can harm our natural resources?

Creating a green society is a key goal of our city. More than 20 percent of Denmark's energy already comes from renewable energy. Trees are renewable energy source and are as important to human as food and water are. Did you know that one tree can clean toxic emissions produced from an average car being driven 4,000 miles?
Can you help me create my next webpage on the ways to renew our natural resources and help reduce pollution?
